item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
I don't know exactly why, but I'm getting strong echoes of V'Ger from the first Star Trek movie.
Something about existing only to learn maybe?

Which suggests one interesting possibility for why enlightenment is lethal. All students are found inadequate, not directly because meat brains can't handle the data flood. But because of the underlying corollary that the minds contained in that meat are not good enough for what The Teacher really wants.
What would happen if a mind (note: not necessarily a brain) did absorb all the knowledge of 606? It fits fridge-logic that the student mind would become a functional copy of the teacher. So "enlightenment" could be a form of reproduction. And 606 kills its pupils because they insist on being disappointing and staying meat-bound instead of metamorphing into baby glow-balls.

item.title: Re: Staff Post - Wikiwalk Proposal
item.content:encoded:
Through use of a mobile remotely operated device, SCP-606 is to be provided with an ordinary USB flash storage device containing no less than 2MB of data every 12 hours. The data contained on the device is to be left to the discretion of SCP-606's supervisor, but text from classic literature or encyclopaedias, movie clips or audio files of historical speeches are ideal. In an emergency situation this may be substituted with 'data' in any form, such as print, compact discs or video tapes. A careful record of all data provided to SCP-606 must be kept. SCP-606 should not be given repeated information except in an emergency situation. No material pertaining to the Foundation or other anomalous objects should be provided to SCP-606 under any circumstances.

This more up to snuff?

item.title: Staff Post - Wikiwalk Proposal
item.content:encoded:
Timer Expired. Edits made as discussed below. Author may revert at any time.

The WikiWalk team is proposing edits to this page. All proposed edits will be in a collapsible below this post, and after 7 days if there are no serious objections to the edits, the feedback received will be taken into account as the edits are made. If you have questions not directly related to the article about this project, please pm a member of the WikiWalk Team

+ Show Block
- Hide Block

Now, if I was Johnny Foundation, I would be very concerned of the implications of SCP-606 accessing SCP-028 and having a literal pool of instantaneous knowledge at its disposal. Best to keep those things as far apart as the Foundation can. As such, I am recommending the following edits:

Changing this:

Through use of a mobile remotely operated device, SCP-606 is to be provided with an ordinary USB flash storage device containing no less than 2MB of data every 12 hours. The data contained on the device is to be left to the discretion of SCP-606's supervisor, but text from classic literature or encyclopaedias, movie clips or audio files of historical speeches are ideal. In an emergency situation this may be substituted with 'data' in any form, such as print, compact discs or video tapes. A careful record of all data provided to SCP-606 must be kept. SCP-606 should not be given repeated information except in an emergency situation. No material pertaining to the Foundation should be provided to SCP-606 under any circumstances.

To this:

Through use of a mobile remotely operated device, SCP-606 is to be provided with an ordinary USB flash storage device containing no less than 2MB of data every 12 hours. The data contained on the device is to be left to the discretion of SCP-606's supervisor, but text from classic literature or encyclopaedias, movie clips or audio files of historical speeches are ideal. In an emergency situation this may be substituted with 'data' in any form, such as print, compact discs or video tapes. A careful record of all data provided to SCP-606 must be kept. SCP-606 should not be given repeated information except in an emergency situation. No material pertaining to the Foundation should be provided to SCP-606, and no personnel who have previously worked with SCP-028 should be assigned to SCP-606, under any circumstances.

If anyone has other/better examples that could be used here please leave a comment saying so!
This was deliciously eerie, glad to give it its 100th upvote.

A good rule of thumb is to double-check your facts before you give suggestions based on them.

I personally love it when people comment on my articles, and I feel that discussion should be encouraged if people are interested. item.title: Staff Post - Open
item.content:encoded:
responding to an individual comment is necroposting, which is against the forum rules

I'm pretty sure staff is totally fine with necroposting so long as the discussion is being moved on in a meaningful way. pastarasta1's comment looks fine here, especially given that it may have cleared up the scenario for other passersby.

There's no chance that Towerator will read this, and even less of a chance that he'd be interested in it.

There's also no way to confirm this. Furthermore, please don't speak for other people if/when they're not around.

And as far as the "in review" thing goes, thats part of the article, the author isn't unsure of what class it needs to be, its the scientists in-universe that are.

It looks like this is what pastarasta1 was saying. Towerator said they should keep it Euclid, and pastarasta1 stated that given that the class was under review in-universe, the class could simply remain Euclid.

Gnago, please refrain from telling other people what to do. This is not the first time staff has needed to correct you.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded: Um, I guess it's okay when you post something to in the thread discussion of an SCP, for example complimenting it or explaining a downvote, but responding to an individual comment is necroposting, which is against the forum rules. There's no chance that Towerator will read this, and even less of a chance that he'd be interested in it. I'm not any sort of authority nor am I 100% sure about the exact rules of necroposting, but I'd suggest not to respond to comments that are 6+ months old, since they most likely won't be seen by the person you're responding to. And as far as the "in review" thing goes, thats part of the article, the author isn't unsure of what class it needs to be, its the scientists in-universe that are. Nevertheless, its good that you're reading plenty of SCPs, so don't take this message as a "hey, you should stop and be intimidated by us" or whatever, it's just a bit of a heads up.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
It's the light of knowledge. I have a soft spot for skips that are puns taken literally, but which the Foundation manages to miss.

If it feeds off information sources, have the Foundation tried withholding nourishment? What happens when they feed it wrong information, contradictory statements, or meaningless data?

If it feeds on (ie. duplicates) a living brain shortly before death, does that mean the owner of the brain gets copied and immortalised in some form? Could this be a clue to the origin and function of 606?

Oh, and is the tonal language related to Solresol?

I think there's a lot of implied questions and possible answers here - and for me that's what makes for a good skip.
